findings.finding: The main grid image and the main_image_brief both show a debossed, hot-stamped 'ECT-32' numeral molded into the cap face - that is idea I1 (Stamped Load-Rating Corner Caps). Genius's recommended_version_id is v1_launch, whose idea_ids are I2, I3, I4, I5 only - I1 is explicitly deferred with a 'stretch' ruling. The single highest-stakes asset (the thumbnail that decides gate.image_orientation and CTR) depicts a feature the funded product will not have.
findings.fix: Rewrite the main image prompt and main_image_brief for the v1_launch configuration: a plain molded safety-blue cap (I3) with no deboss, and move the legible ECT-32 callout onto the pack/card/belly-band (I2) instead of the cap face. Keep the I1 version of the prompt on file for v2, clearly labeled as v2-only.

findings.finding: I1's 'low' prior-art risk rests on the claim that a molded, on-cap ECT numeral 'was not observed on any of scout's four named competitors' - but scout's own gaps explicitly state no competitor thumbnail or main image could be fetched this session ('No competitor thumbnail/main image could be viewed'). This turns an unconfirmed absence into a stated visual fact, exactly the kind of quiet confidence upgrade the run's evidence gap should not survive into a tooling decision.
findings.fix: Reframe the reason as 'no competitor title/bullet text makes this claim' (the only channel scout actually had), mark visual novelty as unconfirmed, and require a manual look at the actual live grid/listing images before the hero tooling spend ($1,500-$6,000) is approved.

findings.finding: Asserts the competitive grid is 'a sea of white-cardboard, white-background competitor tiles' with no fact_id and no caveat. Scout never obtained a single competitor image this session (explicit gap). The entire blue-cap contrast rationale, and the 'high' thumbnail_visibility ratings given to I1 and I3 that genius later uses to justify forecast share, rest on this unverified premise.
findings.fix: Label this as an assumption pending a manual grid check rather than a stated fact; downgrade thumbnail_visibility confidence for I1/I3 until someone actually looks at the live search-results page.

findings.finding: Scout's complaint cluster C1 is explicitly self-flagged as 'Inferred (not directly mined)' from SKU-tier proliferation, not from real review text (see scout.gaps: 'no actual 1-2 star or 5-star review text could be mined ... inferred ... low-confidence'). Buyer's buy_driver.evidence cites C1 as settled reasoning for pain_level ('moderate') without carrying forward that caveat - the reduced-confidence label lives only in buyer.hypotheses_tested, not where the pain-depth judgement itself is made.
findings.fix: Add the inferred-not-confirmed caveat directly to buy_driver.evidence (and to unmet_needs N1/N5, which also trace only to C1/C2), and consider whether pain_level should be presented as a working hypothesis rather than a flat 'moderate' rating until scout gets real review access.

findings.finding: The playbook's '>=15% of negatives = must-fix' rule is applied mechanically to C1 (35%) and C2 (25%), but those percentages are scout's own invented placeholders, not measured shares of real one-star reviews (scout: 'inferred ... not directly mined'). Four of six ideas (I1 hero, I2, I4, I5) and nearly all of the launch tooling/NRE trace back to fixing these two unconfirmed clusters.
findings.fix: Flag C1/C2-derived ideas with a reduced-confidence note, and recommend a scout follow-up pass (actual review mining, once egress is unblocked) before the full v1_launch tooling commitment - or explicitly hedge the must-fix classification in the ideas that depend on it.

findings.finding: The factory-copy obituary (probability 0.35, impact major - the brief's own 'LOW BARRIER to entry' risk) is mitigated at 'genuinely zero' cost by deferring I1's hero mold. But the actually-visible, copyable surface that ships in v1 (I3's blue caps, I4's longer wings, I2's weight-match card) is unaffected by deferring I1 - a competitor can copy the visible v1 product regardless. A high-probability, major-impact risk with a free mitigation that does not address the real copyable surface is exactly the 'mitigations that cost nothing' pattern to flag.
findings.fix: Either name a real, costed anti-copy step (design patent/trademark filing on the wing geometry or card system, faster reorder-to-v2 cadence) or lower confidence that deferring I1 meaningfully reduces this specific risk.

findings.finding: v1_launch's computed unit_weight_g is 258g (~9.1oz), but genius's fba_fee_usd assumption text says the base fee was triangulated 'scaled for the heavier 8oz tier.' The rigid mailer, bundle add-on and card push the actual packed weight past the 8oz assumption baked into the fee derivation, so the FBA fee range may understate the true weight-based fee bracket once all BOM lines are included.
findings.fix: Re-derive fba_fee_usd against the actual 258-260g weight (or trim BOM/packaging weight back under 8oz) before finalizing the economics that price and feasibility rest on.

findings.finding: Price range ($13.99-$16.79, base $15.49) spans only about +/-9% around base - well inside the +/-30% guardrail for anything uncertain, even though price is one of the Monte-Carlo-sampled ranges. It also never tests the buyer's own max_without_reason ceiling ($12.99), despite buyer's three_second_scan rating the price signal 'push_away' against the $13.99 100-pack anchor.
findings.fix: Widen the low end toward $12.99-$13.99 so the Monte Carlo actually samples the discount scenario buyer's own data flags as a live risk, rather than only testing a narrow band near the top of the brief's price ceiling.

findings.finding: The framework defines 'stretch' as exactly one sanity rail broken, named, with a fix. Genius's json asserts 'stretch' but never names, in the structured output, which rail is broken or what the fix is. The base-case ad_rate (40%, a launch-phase figure) is used as the single blended year-1 base rather than being isolated to early months, which plausibly leaves the base-case contribution margin thin - but this is not stated or reconciled anywhere in the json.
findings.fix: State explicitly which sanity rail is broken in the base case (most likely contribution % of price) and give the concrete fix (e.g., front-load review-seeding to cut ad_rate faster, or hold price near the top of the band) rather than leaving the 'stretch' call unexplained.

findings.finding: Unlike complaint_clusters (which at least carry a root_cause_hypothesis explaining the inference chain and fact_ids), praise_clusters carry no fact_ids and no per-item caveat at all - the 'inferred, not mined' admission lives only in the separate top-level gaps array. A downstream reader of praise_clusters alone would reasonably take them as sourced.
findings.fix: Add fact_ids (even pointing only to the category-existence facts) and an explicit inferred-not-mined caveat directly on each praise cluster, matching the treatment complaint_clusters already received.

findings.finding: Assumption text explicitly calls both figures 'stale' / widened per the brief's no-fee-from-memory rule, but neither JSON object sets the 'stale': true flag the output format supports - a downstream reader relying on the flag rather than the prose would miss the caveat.
findings.fix: Set "stale": true on both range objects to match the prose.

findings.finding: States 'Category norm here is a plain poly bag with no printed spec' as a flat market fact with no fact_id. Scout never viewed any competitor packaging or listing image this session, so this specific claim about rival unboxing experience is invented, not observed.
findings.fix: Caveat this as an assumption based on category price-point norms rather than a directly observed fact about competitor packaging.

three_things_the_founder_must_hear: The main product image you're about to approve for photography shows the debossed 'ECT-32' hero cap - but genius's own recommended launch version (v1_launch) does not include that cap. If you shoot and list against that image while shipping v1, you will be selling a product that doesn't match its own thumbnail.

The two complaint patterns (wrong thickness for box weight, and fiddly fit/fold) that justify most of the ideas and nearly all of the launch tooling budget were never mined from a single real review this session - scout's network access was blocked and it said so plainly. Buyer and innovaty both built on top of those guesses without carrying that caveat forward, so the product's core differentiation thesis is an assumption chain, not evidence yet.

Nobody has actually seen a real competitor listing image or the live search grid - the 'blue caps pop against white tiles' visual strategy and the claim that no rival already molds a spec number onto its cap are both invented on top of that same blind spot. A five-minute manual look at the real grid, before committing the $1,500-$6,000 hero-cap tooling decision, would validate or kill this cheaply.
